title.value: Upscaling of Fault Zone Permeability Tensor From Fault Components Permeability Estimations and Numerical

note.value:
Fault zone structures has been well described by detailed geologic mapping in Valley of Fire State National Park. These faults are the consequence of slip along pre-existing joint zones and the resulting fault zone corresponds to damaged zone composed of joints, sheared joints, fault related deformation bands, and fault gouge. Permeability of each of these features has been determined either by mini-permeameter measurements or by petrophysical image analysis and application of Kozeny-Carmen relationship. Apertures for open fractures has been estimated from field observations.

Then, a numerical procedure for the determination of equivalent grid block permeability tensor for heterogeneous porous media has been used to upscale the permeability tensor of blocks around 5 meters side comprising parts of the fault zone. Cross-plot of upscaled permeability calculated for each grid block, as well as the permeability tensor characterizing the whole studied block, are presented.

Results indicate that faults formed by shearing of joint zones have a strongly anisotropic permeability structures. Fault parallel permeability may be increased by up to 2 orders of magnitude relative to the host rock and is a function of the aperture and distribution of orientation of shearing induced joints or splay fractures as well as the matrix permeability that acts as a relay between disconnected clusters of joints and fault segments. Fault normal permeability may be reduced by up to 3 orders of magnitude compared to the host rock which is tied up to the width and continuity of the fault gouge zones as well as the density of deformations bands or small faults within and around the fault.

Principal permeability directions of the upscaled large block may correspond to an average direction between mean joint trend and mean fault core direction for a small amount of slip. At a larger slip amount, principal permeability directions get closer to the mean fault core but can deviate noticeably from this direction. The role of deformation bands on the flow behavior around the fault zone is also pointed out. By taking into account the oversampling of deformation bands, we show that this consideration may have a significant enough role on principal permeability directions.

Also, it will be shown that fault zone permeability varies with slip magnitude. Although increased slip leads to higher density of sheared induce joints, the fault parallel permeability is not necessarily increased because of the strong dispersion in joints orientation. For the same reason, fault normal permeability doesn't necessarily decrease when slip increases, although the number and density of low permeability features such as gouge, sheared joints and deformation bands, increases. As a consequence, for a given size of block, principal permeability values may strongly decrease as slip increases.

Jourde, Herve. (1999). Upscaling of Fault Zone Permeability Tensor From Fault Components Permeability Estimations and Numerical. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: http://purl.stanford.edu/tz439yk2143
